title: Adapter start-up
description: The body of the signed POST /v1/adapter, application/json, that an adapter sends each time it starts: where a person is sent to connect the source, and how often the adapter pulls changes from the source. It is signed with the adapter's access key as definitions.schema.json describes. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, or a request whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401; definitions.schema.json has the replay rule. A member this schema does not define is refused, invalid_request.

version.description: The document format. The control plane refuses a version it does not read.

time.description: When the adapter built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, with an unsigned 401.

connect_url.description: Where the control plane sends a person to connect the source, with the connect pass appended as the query parameter state (connect-pass.schema.json). The URL is opaque to the control plane.

sync.description: How often the adapter pulls changes from the source by default, and the shortest interval it allows. minimum_interval is at most default_interval; the schema cannot say so, and the control plane refuses a sync that breaks it, invalid_request. A person may change the interval in the control plane, and the change feed tells the adapter (changes.schema.json, the sync kind).

default_interval.description: The interval the adapter pulls at unless a person sets another, in seconds, from 60 to 86400.

minimum_interval.description: The shortest interval the adapter allows, in seconds, from 60 to 86400, at most default_interval.

sends_changes.description: true when the adapter sends the source's changes as they happen and pulls only to catch anything missed; false when it learns of changes only by pulling.
